question: How much of the difference between people in how readily they fall into flow is down to their genes?
answer: Roughly a third, by one large twin study. Mosing and colleagues asked thousands of Swedish twins how often they felt flow at work, at home and at leisure. Identical twins resembled each other more than non-identical ones, putting the heritable share at roughly 30%. The rest lay in experiences not shared.
move: A trait can run in families without being settled at birth.

diagram.caption: Twins put roughly 30% of the differences in flow down to genes.

source: Mosing et al., Twin Res Hum Genet, 2012
reference: Mosing, Magnusson, Pedersen, Nakamura, Madison & Ullén, Heritability of proneness for psychological flow experiences, Twin Research and Human Genetics, 2012
